name: Chen Naga
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2024 (pre-publication copy; Zenodo record 22253033, posted 2026-09-02, CC BY 4.0). Patkaian (Northern Naga). Chapter for Hildebrandt, Modi, Peterson & Suzuki (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Tibeto-Burman Languages. 34 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 3.1-3.1.1 (branch-level): Patkaian varieties share a sesquisyllabic CəCV[CN] syllable structure; 'The majority of Patkaian varieties have a system of lexical tone.. between three and five lexical tones'; 'many Patkaian varieties lack detailed tonal descriptions'. Chen (Kyan) appears only in the *z- reflex table, pronoun tables and subgrouping (Southwestern Patkaian, spoken on both sides of the border). No word-stress statement for Chen or for the branch.

sources.citation: Konyak, Hoipo. 2021. A First Look at Chen (Konyak) Argument and Clause Structures. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 14.1: i-xi. hdl:10524/52480 (downloaded via Internet Archive copy of the eVols bitstream; live bitstream could not be reached by automated download).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the 11 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent + read). Only prosodic statement is footnote 1, p. ii: 'Tones in Chen are represented by numbers: Low = [22], Mid = unmarked.' Examples carry 22 tone marks. Syntax data paper (NP structure, pronouns, simple clauses); data from Chen Hoyat village, Lahe township, Myanmar; author is a native speaker (Payap University).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-050 and New Code Request form for [nqq] Naga, Kyan-Karyaw (adopted 2013-01-23). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing linguistic beyond classification; background only (about 13 villages, about 9,000 speakers in northern Lahe township; evidence = unpublished SIL/LSDO sociolinguistic surveys of 2006 and 2012 with wordlists; published sources cited are ethnographic: Saul 2005, Stirn & van Ham 2003).

sources.citation: Nagaraja, K. S. 2010. Konyak Grammar. Mysore: CIIL. (already held by the project under kony1248; checked only for mentions of Chen)
sources.note: Describes standard (Wakching-based) Konyak [kony1248], not Chen; scanned text has no mention of Chen. Not a source for chen1271.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2025. On the independence of tonogenesis in Patkaian branches. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 48(2): 163-192.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Comparative tonal phonology of the whole Patkaian group including Southwestern varieties (Chen/Kyan is in his sample); would confirm the Chen tone inventory and may comment on syllable prominence in sesquisyllables.

sources.citation: Konyak, Hoipo. (to appear per Konyak 2021; c. 2021-2022) A preliminary grammar of Chen, a Konyak language of India and Myanmar. MA thesis, Department of Linguistics, Payap University, Chiang Mai.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only full description of Chen announced in print, by a native-speaker linguist; a Payap grammar thesis normally opens with a phonology chapter (syllable, tone, word prosody) and is the one place a stress/accent statement for Chen would be made. Would supersede the JSEALS footnote.

sources.citation: SIL International / LSDO Myanmar. 2006, 2012. Unpublished sociolinguistic survey reports and wordlists of Kyan (Chen) and Karyaw Naga, Lahe township (cited as the evidence base in ISO 639-3 CR 2012-050).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other first-hand data collection on Myanmar Chen; survey wordlists are usually tone-transcribed and reports sometimes include a phonology note. Low chance of a stress statement.
